generator.params.frond_length.why: A fern's frond is its blade and its stipe, the leaf's stalk, end to end.

generator.params.stipe.why: The bare share of a frond's length is its stipe's.

generator.params.pinna_length.why: A blade is as broad as its longest pair of pinnae reach out from the rachis, one each side; pinnae standing well out from the rachis reach nearly their whole length, and the program sizes them by the frond's length.

generator.params.pieces.why: The program hangs two pairs of pinnae on each piece of the rachis above the stipe, so a frond with as many pinnae as its flora counts has a quarter as many blade pieces, and the stipe's pieces besides.

appearance.organs.*.shape.width.why: A once-divided frond's pinnae stand side by side along its blade, each as broad as the gap from one pinna to the next, and as long as half the blade is wide.

generator.params.frond_life.why: A deciduous fern's fronds die in their first winter, a year from when they unroll; an evergreen fern's live as long as its leaves are stated to.

appearance.organs.*.shape.divided.why: A frond's pinnae are drawn by the program and each pinna by its card, so a twice-divided frond's pinna card is divided once and a frond divided three times draws its pinnules divided again.

traits.reproduction.note: Ferns and horsetails are seedless vascular plants: they spread by spores shed from sporangia, not by seeds (Biology 2e, 25.4).

rules.note: What the fern program's parameters and the frond card mean: frond_length is the whole frond, stipe included, and stipe the share of it without pinnae; frond_life is a frond's years; the program draws the frond's first division as pinnae, so the pinna card shows the divisions below it. Floras measure a fern's blade and stipe apart, so the frond is their sum.
